item.title: Can Europe Afford Its Welfare State?
item.description:
Wall Street Week • Nov 8th, 2026
Can Europe Afford Its Welfare State?
Europe’s postwar welfare state was built for a younger, growing population. Today, aging communities are putting pensions, health care and public finances under mounting strain. As governments try to fund defense, infrastructure and education at the same time, the fight over who pays is spilling into politics and the streets.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
President Donald Trump’s return to the White House changed the political calculus around mergers and acquisitions, reviving companies’ desire for dream deals that had become difficult to pull off. Now, corporate America is on the clock.
The rout by the Democrats in the midterms is creating a sudden sense of urgency in boardrooms, with executives wondering if they might have one last chance to pull off a transformational transaction while M&A-friendly regulators remain in place under Trump.

item.title: Democratic Sweep Tests Trump-Linked Trades Across Latin America
item.description: Investors who spent the past year factoring countries’ standing with Donald Trump into their Latin America trades are confronting a new variable: a Democratic-controlled US Congress.

item.title: How Everyday Apps Feed Police Surveillance
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg investigative journalist Ryan Gallagher explains how location data collected through everyday smartphone apps can ultimately be sold to law enforcement agencies, often without users knowing where their information ends up. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gallagher details how Penlink’s surveillance technology can track phones using commercially obtained data and why its use has fueled calls for greater privacy protections and oversight. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Poland Probes Krakow Shooting as Terrorism
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News reporter Piotr Skolimowski discusses the investigation into the deadly Krakow shooting and the far right ideology authorities say may have motivated the attack. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Skolimowski explains how the shooting comes amid heightened political tensions in Poland and growing divisions over the war in Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What America’s Factories Reveal About the Economy
item.description: Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin traveled to Union, South Carolina, to hear directly from manufacturers about what is happening beneath the economic data. At auto-parts maker Gestamp, demand remains solid and investment continues, but businesses are navigating rising costs, changing technology and an uncertain policy environment, giving Barkin a ground-level view of the forces shaping the economy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gabon Seeks $2 Billion to Revive Mabounie Rare Earths Project
item.description: Gabon is looking to revive its long-stalled Mabounié niobium and rare-earth project through a proposed $2 billion development involving Emirati-backed New Energy Metals and the Chinese engineering group ENFI.
